en.title: Airbus partnerships propel veterans into civilian careers
en.summary: Airbus has announced two partnerships with veteran service organizations to help former US service members move into civilian aerospace roles, building on its SkillBridge program at the Mobile, Alabama manufacturing facility.
body: Transitioning from military service to a civilian career can be a challenging journey, but for US Army veteran Chayse Teague, Airbus' partnership with the US Department of Defense's SkillBridge program made the move seamless. Teague spent 12 years as a Blackhawk helicopter mechanic in the US Army and now works as a Flight Line Quality Assurance Inspector for Airbus' A320 Family aircraft at the Airbus US Manufacturing Facility in Mobile, Alabama, ensuring the safety and quality of commercial aircraft delivered from the site. "One of the things the military teaches you is problem-solving and attention to detail, which is huge in a quality assurance role," Teague said. Teague is one of four recent participants in the SkillBridge program at the facility, each of whom has landed a full-time role.

US Coast Guard veteran Hunter Montgomery joined Airbus as a technician for the autonomous drilling units used to assemble aircraft after a six-year military career in search and rescue and equipment maintenance. Evan Roper, who previously calibrated avionics equipment on C-17s in the US Air Force, now works on Mobile's ground test inspection team. "Skillbridge is a great transition tool because you essentially have a working interview for three to four months doing the exact job you'll be doing if hired full time," Roper said.

To help more service members find similar success, Airbus recently announced two strategic partnerships with Heroes MAKE America and Hiring Our Heroes. "Partnering with organizations like Hiring Our Heroes and Heroes Make America reflects our deep commitment to those who have served our Nation," said Caroline Jecko-Parkes, Head of Human Resources for Airbus in North America. The Manufacturing Institute's Heroes MAKE America program helps employers access transitioning service members, veterans and military spouses, while the US Chamber of Commerce Foundation's Hiring Our Heroes program reaches nearly 270,000 transitioning service members per year. The SkillBridge program allows transitioning service members to spend up to their final 180 days of active duty gaining civilian work experience while continuing to receive full military pay and benefits.

zh.title: 空中巴士攜手退伍軍人組織：協助退役軍人轉任民航製造工作
zh.summary: 空中巴士宣布與兩個退伍軍人服務組織合作，協助退役美軍轉任民航製造職務，延續其在阿拉巴馬州莫比爾廠區推行的SkillBridge計畫。
body: 從軍旅轉任民間職涯並不容易，但對美國陸軍退役軍人Chayse Teague而言，空中巴士與美國國防部SkillBridge計畫的合作讓轉換相當順利。Teague在陸軍擔任黑鷹直升機機務人員12年，如今在空中巴士位於阿拉巴馬州莫比爾的美國製造廠區擔任A320系列飛機的飛機線品質保證檢查員，負責把關廠區交付商用飛機的安全與品質。Teague是該廠區近期4名SkillBridge計畫參與者之一，4人皆已取得全職職位。
美國海岸防衛隊退役軍人Hunter Montgomery服役6年、從事搜救與裝備維修，退役後加入空中巴士，擔任組裝飛機用自動鑽孔設備的技術員。曾在美國空軍負責校準C-17運輸機航電設備的Evan Roper，如今在莫比爾廠區的地面測試檢查團隊工作。Roper表示，SkillBridge是很好的轉換工具，因為參與者等於有3到4個月的實作面試，做的正是獲聘全職後的工作內容。

為協助更多退役軍人獲得類似機會，空中巴士近期宣布與Heroes MAKE America及Hiring Our Heroes建立兩項策略合作。空中巴士北美人力資源主管Caroline Jecko-Parkes表示，與這類組織合作展現公司對退役軍人的深切承諾。製造業協會的Heroes MAKE America計畫協助雇主接觸正在轉換跑道的軍人、退伍軍人與軍眷；美國商會基金會的Hiring Our Heroes計畫每年觸及近27萬名轉換跑道的軍人。SkillBridge計畫讓即將退役的軍人在退伍前最多180天內，到民間企業累積工作經驗，期間仍領取全額軍餉與福利。

Hunter Montgomery, a US Coast Guard veteran, joined Airbus as a technician for the autonomous drilling units used to assemble aircraft; Evan Roper, a former US Air Force avionics calibrator on C-17s, now works on Mobile's ground test inspection team.
